title: The frontend lets a user save and leave from every journey question page; DR1 offers that on most of its pages but not on seven of them, and DR1 does not say which is right.

finding.frontend: Every journey page that offers a save action offers the same three, from one shared partial (`src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13`): a primary "Save and continue", a secondary "Save and return to hub" and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. That is 24 of the 40 captured screens. Sixteen do not carry them, and eleven of those are pages where they would make no sense — the three task-list states, the two dashboards, the review, the declaration, the confirmation, the check-answers pair and the delete and cancel-amend confirmations. That leaves one group of journey question pages that asks a question and offers no way to save and leave: the five address pickers, which end with "Save and continue" on its own.
finding.prototype: DR1 offers the equivalent pair on 26 of its 42 screens. Sixteen do not carry it, and nine of those are again pages where it would make no sense — the four dashboard states, the task list, the declaration, the submitted page and the two review states. The remaining seven are journey question pages, and they end in three different ways. Origin of the import and CPH number end with "Save and continue" alone (`app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:167-175`). The address select page ends with "Save and continue" and a secondary "Add a new address". The two add-a-transporter detail forms, commercial and private, end with "Save and continue" and a secondary "Cancel and return to dashboard" — which returns to the notification list, not to the task list. The transporter-type page and the contact address page end with a bare "Continue". Set against the pairing, five pairs that match screen for screen diverge: origin, CPH number, transporter type, the private transporter form and the contact address page all let a frontend user save and leave where their DR1 counterpart does not. The address pickers are not among them, because neither side offers it there.
finding.difference: There is nothing to build until somebody says which side is right, which is why this is banded disputed rather than as work. DR1 is not consistent with itself here: 26 of its pages carry the pair and seven journey question pages do not, and nothing in the evidence separates the two groups — they are not one section, not one journey branch, and not one kind of question. DR1 is not even consistent within the seven: two end with "Save and continue" alone, two end with "Save and continue" and a cancel that goes to the dashboard rather than the task list, one adds an unrelated secondary, and two end with a bare "Continue" that does not use the word save at all. The frontend's behaviour is a superset of DR1's rather than a contradiction of it, so removing the actions from those five pages would make the service worse if DR1's omission is drift rather than intent. What settles it: a designer saying whether every journey page should let a user save and return to the task list, or whether those specific pages are deliberately continue-only. If the answer is "every page", DR1 needs updating and the frontend is already correct; if it is "only some", the rule that picks them needs writing down before anything is removed, and it has to account for the four wordings DR1 uses across the seven.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a "Save and return to overview" action on DR1's origin of the import, CPH number or add-a-private-transporter pages.
finding.verification: Re-counted both sides from the rendered DOM, listed the button labels on every DR1 screen that lacks the pair, opened the fe-origin and dr1-origin-of-the-import full-page shots, and read save-actions.njk:3-13 and origin-of-the-import.html:167-175. The two headline counts hold — 24 of 40 frontend screens and 26 of 42 DR1 screens — and the falsifier does not fire: none of DR1's origin, CPH number or add-a-private-transporter pages carries "Save and return to overview". The dispute itself is real and is the honest answer here, and re-deriving it made it stronger rather than weaker: DR1 does not merely omit the pair on some pages, it ends those pages four different ways. The difference slot already named the observation that would settle it — a designer saying whether every journey page should offer it — so the dispute is stated well enough for somebody to close. Band stays `disputed`. Three counts inside the slots were wrong; see the correction.
finding.correction: The band and the conclusion stand. Three claims inside the slots did not. First, `frontend` said "The only screens that do not are the five address pickers". Sixteen of the 40 do not: the five pickers plus fe-hub, fe-hub-no-commodity, fe-hub-exit-details-blocked, fe-dashboard-empty, fe-dashboard-populated, fe-check-answers, fe-check-answers-submitted, fe-declaration, fe-confirmation, fe-delete-notification and fe-cancel-amend. The pickers are the only journey question pages among them, which is what the sentence meant, so the slot was narrowed to say that rather than struck. Second, `prototype` said DR1's omission covers "the two add-a-transporter pages"; there are three add-a-transporter views — transporter-add, transporter-add-commercial and transporter-add-private — and they do not behave alike: transporter-add ends with a bare "Continue" while the other two end with "Save and continue" and a secondary "Cancel and return to dashboard". Third, and this is the one that mattered, `prototype` and `difference` both said three pairs diverge. Five do. Against pairs.cjs the divergent pairs are fe-origin/dr1-origin-of-the-import, fe-cph-number/dr1-cph-number, fe-transporter-private/dr1-transporter-add-private, fe-transporter-type/dr1-transporter-add and fe-contact/dr1-contact-address-for-consignment — the last two were visible in the original prose but not counted, and dr1-consignment-address-select was counted as a divergence when it is not one, because the frontend's five address pickers do not offer the actions either. Slots rewritten with all seven DR1 pages and their four endings enumerated, since the inconsistency is the whole substance of the dispute.

relatedTo.why: Same two actions. That finding is about what they are called and is settled; this one is about which pages show them and is not.
